issues.body: `LABEL_WRITE_PATTERNS` still requires an explicit `-X/--method POST|PUT|PATCH|DELETE` for `/labels` API calls. GitHub CLI automatically changes the method to POST when fields are supplied, so `gh api repos/$R/issues/$N/labels -f 'labels[]=needs:user'` mutates labels but is not classified as a label-writing step. A foreign PAT in that step consequently escapes R1. The self-test remains at four positives and six negatives and does not exercise this path, so the central invariant is still bypassable.
issues.fix_hint: Classify `gh api` `/labels` calls as mutating when `-f`, `-F`, `--raw-field`, `--field`, or applicable `--input` usage causes the CLI's implicit POST, while excluding explicit or genuine GET requests. Add positive fixtures for explicit-method and implicit-default-POST label writes and a negative genuine-GET fixture.
issues.title: Default-POST `gh api` label writes still bypass the identity guard

verdict.summary: Round 2 is stagnant: the round-1 security finding remains materially unchanged. The classifier still recognizes a mutating `gh api .../labels` call only when `-X/--method POST|PUT|PATCH|DELETE` is explicit, while GitHub CLI implicitly uses POST when request fields or input are supplied. The self-test still has only four positive and six negative fixtures and adds no explicit-method, implicit-default-POST, or genuine-GET coverage. Therefore a standard label write using a foreign PAT can still bypass R1.
